name: C12-6
question: Should Hong Kong tighten rent control on subdivided units? Take a position and defend it with evidence from the course archive.

turns.text: ok so i'm working on this thing about subdivided flats in HK and rent control — need to actually see the sources. can you pull up some docs for me to start? anything on the basic situation of subdivided units

Before I point you anywhere, what do you need a source to *do* here — back up a specific claim you're making about the situation, or give you a first-hand account, or something else? And which claim would it be supporting?

hmm fair question. two things really — i want the raw numbers on how many households are in subdivided units and what they're paying, plus i guess a tenant's own account? not sure yet. just give me whatever's out there on the basic situation first and i'll sort it

Here are some places to look, in no particular order:
- D6: Working Paper: Rent Control and Supply Elasticity in Marginal Housing (Academic working paper). Academic working paper modelling rent control and supply elasticity, arguing theory predicts contraction but magnitude is empirical.
- D2: SDU Rent and Stock Index, 2019–2025 (excerpt) (Data excerpt). Data excerpt giving SDU stock and rent index time series 2019-2025 with stated data caveats.
- D1: Subdivided Housing in Hong Kong: A Primer (Policy brief). Policy brief primer giving overview of SDU situation, tenant profile, and rent-control debate framing.
- D3: Tenant Interview: Mr Chan, Kwai Chung (Interview). First-person tenant interview with a Kwai Chung delivery driver, dated to current policy debate.
- D4: Tenant Interview: Mrs Wong, Sham Shui Po (Interview). First-person tenant interview with an elderly Sham Shui Po tenant, including interviewer-noted contradictions.
Pick one or more (by id) and tell me why.
want numbers plus tenant accounts first

Unlocked: D1 (Subdivided Housing in Hong Kong: A Primer), D2 (SDU Rent and Stock Index, 2019–2025 (excerpt)), D3 (Tenant Interview: Mr Chan, Kwai Chung), D4 (Tenant Interview: Mrs Wong, Sham Shui Po). You can now read their passages by id, for example D1p1.
need supply evidence and stock figures
Unlocked: D6 (Working Paper: Rent Control and Supply Elasticity in Marginal Housing), D2 (SDU Rent and Stock Index, 2019–2025 (excerpt)). You can now read their passages by id, for example D6p1.
ok last gap — the legal side and enforcement. anything on compensation claims from a hard cap, and inspection capacity? think it was a lawyer's memo and a subcommittee note

You've named the two things you want covered — compensation claims and inspection capacity — but not yet what each must prove for your argument. Which claim in your essay would each of those sources be there to support?

right, sorry — what i need is: the memo to back up that a hard cap risks compensation claims while an indexed per-sq-ft band can be defended as rate-capping; and the subcommittee note to back up that enforcement is too thin (inspection under 6% a year, register costing 40-60 staff-years) and that it'd miss the tenants with no written agreement / newest arrivals. so like supporting the 'enforcement can't protect the tail' point

Here are some places to look, in no particular order:
- D6: Working Paper: Rent Control and Supply Elasticity in Marginal Housing (Academic working paper). Academic working paper modeling supply elasticity; distinguishes first- vs second-generation controls and projects contraction effects.
- D11: NGO Report: Rehousing Pathways First (NGO report). NGO report from tenant survey; argues against hard caps, favoring tenure security and light banding.
- D4: Tenant Interview: Mrs Wong, Sham Shui Po (Interview). First-person tenant interview; elderly long-term SDU resident describing no written agreement and landlord behavior.
- D10: Internal Minute: Housing Authority Enforcement Subcommittee (draft, not for circulation) (Internal minute). Internal subcommittee minute (draft); enforcement vantage on inspection capacity, register costs, and missed tail.
- D9: Legal Opinion: Compensation and Judicial Review Risk (Legal opinion). Lawyer's legal opinion; assesses compensation and judicial review risk of hard cap versus indexed per-sq-ft band.
Pick one or more (by id) and tell me why.
legal compensation risk and enforcement capacity, both needed for the hard-cap objection

Unlocked: D9 (Legal Opinion: Compensation and Judicial Review Risk), D10 (Internal Minute: Housing Authority Enforcement Subcommittee (draft, not for circulation)). You can now read their passages by id, for example D9p1.
